jobs.title: Director of Data Architecture
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director of Data Architecture based in Canada.

The Director of Data Architecture will define and lead the organization's long-term data strategy, overseeing the architecture, infrastructure, and teams responsible for managing its entire data ecosystem. You will drive the development of scalable data platforms, ensuring seamless data integration, transformation, storage, and delivery across multiple systems. Leading two specialized functions, Data Engineering and Data Operations Engineering, you will balance innovation with the reliability and performance of existing production environments. This position combines strategic leadership with hands-on technical involvement, particularly during the initial stages of team development. You will work closely with executive and engineering leaders to establish architectural standards and align data initiatives with broader business objectives. You will also play a central role in strengthening data quality, governance, security, and compliance while building a robust data foundation that supports analytics, product innovation, and business growth.

Accountabilities

Define and lead the long-term data architecture and platform strategy, overseeing data warehouses, operational data stores, and the evolution toward a modern medallion-based lakehouse architecture (bronze, silver, and gold layers).
Design, develop, and manage data lake and warehouse infrastructure, including the creation and optimization of data marts supporting analytics, product development, and business reporting.
Establish architecture standards and orchestration strategies for all data workflows, including source ingestion, web-scraping pipelines, ETL/ELT processes, and automated workflow management.
Oversee the infrastructure, administration, capacity planning, reliability, and cost optimization of data warehouses and pipelines.
Develop and enforce comprehensive data governance frameworks covering data quality, lineage, access controls, classification, retention, and auditability.
Build, lead, and scale two complementary teams: Data Engineering, responsible for developing new pipelines and architecture, and Data Operations Engineering, responsible for maintaining and optimizing existing production processes.
Define the organizational structure and leadership model as the teams grow, determining when additional management layers and operational responsibilities are required.
Remain hands-on during the initial stages by designing and reviewing pipelines, data models, and orchestration processes, while progressively empowering teams to manage execution independently.
Maintain strong technical oversight to guide architectural decisions and ensure the continuous evolution of the data platform.
Collaborate with engineering leadership and the CTO to establish technical direction, align data architecture with company-wide standards, and support strategic technology decisions.
Partner with product, analytics, data engineering, and business stakeholders to understand data requirements and translate them into effective warehouse and data mart solutions.
Establish and monitor data quality controls, lineage tracking, and auditability standards across all data pipelines.
Oversee data access policies, classification standards, and retention practices to ensure secure and compliant data management.
Ensure that compliance-sensitive and audit-relevant information is managed appropriately as data sources and customer requirements expand.

Requirements

At least 10 years of professional experience in data engineering, data architecture, or related technical fields, including a minimum of 5 years in Director- or Manager-level leadership positions with responsibility for architecture strategy and team management.
Extensive hands-on experience designing, implementing, and operating cloud-based data warehouse or lakehouse architectures, particularly with Snowflake and/or BigQuery.
Strong understanding and practical experience with medallion architecture patterns, including bronze, silver, and gold data layers.
Experience integrating multiple source systems, including MongoDB, PostgreSQL, and MySQL, and developing ingestion and ETL pipelines from diverse structured and unstructured data sources.
Experience building and managing web-scraping pipelines, background processing systems, and automated workflow orchestration.
Proven ability to establish, develop, and scale data engineering or data platform organizations, including structuring separate engineering and operations functions.
Strong knowledge of data governance frameworks, with experience establishing and enforcing standards for data quality, lineage, access management, and retention in regulated or compliance-sensitive environments.
Demonstrated ability to define technical strategy in collaboration with senior engineering leaders and influence architectural decisions across multiple teams.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to present technical strategy, platform performance, infrastructure costs, and operational risks directly to executive leadership, including the CTO.
Strong strategic thinking, organizational leadership, and problem-solving abilities, combined with the willingness to remain technically involved when needed.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience consolidating, modernizing, or re-architecting data platforms following acquisitions or significant expansions in data sources.
Familiarity with data orchestration and transformation tools such as Airflow and dbt.
Experience designing and managing large-scale web-scraping and crawling infrastructure.
Background developing data marts and self-service analytics platforms for non-technical stakeholders.
Familiarity with data observability and quality monitoring tools such as Monte Carlo, Great Expectations, Soda, or similar solutions.

Benefits

Competitive annual salary: USD 200,000 per year.
Remote work flexibility: Opportunity to work remotely from Canada.
Strategic leadership opportunity: Shape the long-term data architecture and technology strategy of a growing organization.
Team-building experience: Build, lead, and develop two specialized engineering functions while influencing organizational structure and growth.
Technical innovation: Work with modern cloud data platforms, lakehouse architectures, data orchestration, and advanced governance solutions.
Executive collaboration: Partner directly with senior engineering leadership and contribute to high-level technology decisions.
Professional development: Drive large-scale data transformation initiatives while expanding your leadership and technical influence.

How Jobgether Works

to ensure your application is reviewed quickly, objectively, and fairly against the role's core requirements. Our system identifies the top-fitting candidates, and this shortlist is then shared directly with the hiring company. The final decision and next steps (interviews, assessments) are managed by their internal team.

We appreciate your interest and wish you the best!

Why Apply Through Jobgether?

Data Privacy Notice:
By submitting your application, you acknowledge that Jobgether will process your personal data to evaluate your candidacy and share relevant information with the hiring employer. This processing is based on legitimate interest and pre-contractual measures under applicable data protection laws (including GDPR). You may exercise your rights (access, rectification, erasure, objection) at any time.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

jobs.title: Vice President, Finance & Business Operations
jobs.description:
CONTEXT

At Make-A-Wish^® Canada
, we’re redefining how the world perceives wishes through our transformative new brand platform: Wishes Are Medicine.
Grounded in research, this platform recognizes what we’ve long known to be true — that wishes have measurable healing power. When prescribed alongside medical treatment, wishes reduce stress, elevate endorphins, limit emergency room visits, and deliver lasting health benefits.

With more than 3,500 children still waiting
and a new child diagnosed with a critical illness in Canada every two hours, our mission has never been more urgent — and there are many more prescriptions to fill.

To meet this challenge, we’ve launched our new three-year strategic plan — Wishes Are Medicine: One Team, One Mission
— focused intentionally on financial sustainability, mission impact, and operational excellence. When a child is facing a critical illness, a wish isn’t just a moment of joy — it’s a medically supported turning point. Studies show that children who receive a wish are 2.5 times less likely
to have unplanned hospital visits and 1.9 times less likely
to need the ER, with 100% of physicians agreeing that a wish can be a pivotal moment in treatment.

At Make-A-Wish Canada, you can play a lead role in bringing these powerful prescriptions to life. Where Wishes Are Medicine
, transformation becomes a pathway to healing at scale — and this role is your opportunity to architect that future.

Our ambition to reach more children and families requires a strong financial and operational foundation. As Vice President, Finance & Business Operations
, you will help shape that foundation, bringing strategic leadership to financial planning, investments, risk, governance and the services that enable our organization to thrive. You will turn insight into action, strengthen how resources are invested and managed, and help build a more resilient, disciplined and mission-driven organization.

At Make-A-Wish Canada
, you’ll join a team united by a shared mission and an unwavering sense of possibility. Every role — whether advancing fundraising, brand, operations, or technology — helps fuel the same trajectory: transforming how hope and healing come to life for children and families nationwide. If you’re ready to help build a future where every eligible child receives the wish that helps them heal, we invite you to read on.

Role Overview

We’re seeking a Vice President, Finance & Business Operations
, a strategic and forward-thinking leader who will help shape the next chapter of Make-A-Wish Canada. This is more than a finance role; it’s an opportunity to strengthen the financial and operational foundation that will enable our mission to grow sustainably.

As a key member of our Senior Leadership Team, and reporting to the Senior Vice President, Transformation & Operations, you will bring together financial strategy, business operations, analytics, risk and governance to strengthen how we plan, invest and make decisions. You’ll provide the insight and discipline to steward our resources responsibly, improve organizational performance, and build the capabilities needed to support sustainable growth and greater mission impact.

If you bring financial acumen, business curiosity and enterprise thinking, and believe the strongest organizations pair ambition with discipline, this is your opportunity to help build the foundation from which our mission can grow and bring the power of Wishes Are Medicine to more children and families across Canada.

This is a full-time, permanent, hybrid
role. The hiring range is $145,000-$170,000.

What You Will Do

Shape Financial Strategy:
Lead budgeting, forecasting, multi-year financial planning, and financial modelling. Translate insights into scenarios and recommendations that guide sustainable, mission-aligned decisions over a three-to-five-year time horizon.

Steward Assets and Investments:
Oversee financial assets, treasury, and investment portfolio performance in accordance with policy, ensuring disciplined stewardship and informed decision-making.

Strengthen Governance and Reporting:
Provide clear financial reporting to the Board of Directors and Senior Leadership Team, support the Finance & Audit Committee, and ensure sound governance, audit readiness, and compliance with CRA and other regulatory obligations.

Advance Enterprise Risk Management:
Maintain the enterprise risk register, strengthen internal controls, and lead business continuity and disaster recovery planning to protect the organization’s assets, reputation, and long-term sustainability.

Modernize Financial Capability:
Build stronger modelling, analytics, systems, and processes that improve forecasting, performance visibility, operational efficiency, and organizational decision-making.

Lead Business Services:
Oversee property management, leases, contracts, insurance, and related business services. Balance operational efficiency and financial sustainability with investments in organizational capability and a safe, supportive workplace.

Oversee Gift and Donation Administration:
Ensure sound systems and processes for restricted giving, endowments, estates, and other complex giving structures, coordinating closely with development teams to support stewardship and compliance.

Advise and Partner:
Serve as a trusted advisor to the Senior Vice President, Transformation & Operations, the CEO, and leadership colleagues on finance, risk, and business operations. Bring an enterprise lens to strategic planning and execution.

Guide and Develop Talent:
Build, coach, and lead a high-performing Finance and Business Operations team, creating clarity, accountability, collaboration, and opportunities for growth.

Champion One Team Leadership:
Model One Team, One Mission leadership by working across functions and geographies, breaking down silos, celebrating collective wins, and leading with empathy, inclusion, accountability, and purpose.

Represent the Mission:
Act as a visible and trusted ambassador with auditors, advisors, donors, partners, community leaders, and other stakeholders, supporting the Foundation’s presence and mission across Canada.

What You Bring

You’re a strategic finance leader who pairs sound technical judgment with business curiosity and a hands-on approach. You move with ease between long-term vision and operational detail, helping leaders see the story behind the numbers and make bold, disciplined choices that bring the power of wishes to more children.

Proven Financial Leadership:
10+ years of progressive leadership in nonprofit financial management, with a track record of stewarding complex budgets, investments, assets, and financial operations in service of a bigger mission.

Strategic
Insight
:
Demonstrated strength in financial planning, forecasting, scenario analysis, and investment and treasury management, building the modelling capability that connects strategy, data, and execution.

Strong Credentials:
A CPA designation, supported by a bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business, or a related field, equipping you to lead with rigour and credibility.

Governance and Compliance Expertise:
Advanced knowledge of nonprofit financial management, CRA requirements, GAAP, audits, internal controls, insurance, and board and committee governance — the discipline that protects trust in our mission.

Enterprise Risk and Business Operations Excellence:
Experience in enterprise risk management, business continuity, procurement, contracts, property, insurance, and service delivery across a national or multi-site organization, building a resilient foundation for growth.

Gift Administration Knowledge:
Experience overseeing restricted giving, endowments, estates, and other complex donation structures, with a deep understanding of donor stewardship and the financial processing that honours every gift.

Collaborative People Leadership:
A track record of recruiting, coaching, and developing multidisciplinary teams, building trust across functions and rallying people around shared goals.

Clear and Credible Communication:
The ability to turn complex financial and risk information into practical insight for executives, board members, auditors, volunteers, donors, and cross-functional partners.

Inspiring,
Values-Driven Leadership:
Deep alignment with our mission and a commitment to responsible stewardship, inclusion, and collaboration — a spirit that motivates teams, breaks down silos, and creates life-changing experiences for children and families facing critical illnesses.

How To Apply

If everything you’ve read so far sounds like you, we encourage you to apply
. Please visit the Make-A-Wish Canada candidate portal for current posting details and the application deadline.

Join Our Team - Make-A-Wish Canada

Make-A-Wish Canada
provides equal opportunity in employment and encourages applications from all qualified candidates. Reasonable accommodations due to disability are available on request at any stage of the hiring process.

OUR COMMITMENT TO IDEA

Make-A-Wish Canada is committed to Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, and Access (IDEA)
. We believe it is essential to our mission that we build a diverse, balanced, and vibrant workforce that reflects the communities we serve and seek to serve. Research has shown that candidates from underrepresented groups often apply only when they feel 100% qualified. Even if you do not see yourself fully reflected in every requirement, we still encourage you to apply.

RECRUITMENT PROCESS

Once applications are reviewed, shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Our typical process includes a phone screen, one or two interviews, reference checking, an offer, and a criminal background check for the successful candidate. We thank all applicants for their interest in working with us.

jobs.title: Director, Model Inference Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Description

Thomson Reuters Labs is the global research and development division of Thomson Reuters. We bring together scientists, engineers, and domain experts to explore emerging technologies and develop state-of-the-art AI products, bridging frontier science with practical application. Labs builds and ships custom models for professional workflows requiring fiduciary-grade AI. The Thomson LLM model family was developed by training leading open-weight models on decades of authoritative Thomson Reuters content, with thousands of hours of subject-matter-expert input. Owning the model layer is how we earn trust in the most regulated, highest-stakes professional workflows.

Mariner, Thomson Reuters' custom inference platform, serves every production call to the Thomson model family and is scaling to new product integrations and business lines. This Director, Model Inference Engineering role leads and grows the team that owns the platform, working with senior technical leadership and a cross-functional team to ensure production footing, cost-tracking, compliance, and capacity planning as we scale. You'll lead the inference-engineering team and partner closely with research and product stakeholders, so the serving stack keeps pace with new model releases and product expansion.

For more on the latest model release, see the Thomson 1.0 Technical Report on Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/spaces/tri-fair-lab/publications/blob/main/Thomson_1_0_Technical_Report.pdf

Key Responsibilities

Grow the inference-engineering team: set the hiring bar, run performance and growth conversations, retain in a competitive market, and build an effective and sustainable operating rhythm (on-call, incident reviews, onboarding) as the system expands internationally.
Own delivery of Mariner's engineering roadmap: work with technical leadership, engineers, and researchers to plan and resource against objectives and key results, driving product integrations and international deployment while balancing cost/latency targets.
Scale Thomson's production footing: drive the ISO 27001 compliance path, deliver clean cost-tracking and attribution for Finance, and run GPU-capacity contingency planning so a capacity change doesn't force downtime or costly parallel running.
Represent inference-engineering tradeoffs (cost vs. latency vs. reliability) to senior leadership and cross-functional partners.
Ensure token-economics benchmarks are produced and published, showing Thomson's cost advantage over closed-model APIs when the numbers support it.

Required Qualifications

Production ML-serving depth. You've led or managed inference infrastructure for large models at real production traffic and scale, not just in a research or prototype setting, with wins delivered by teams you led that you can point to, and the fluency to hire, coach, and defend the work.
Infrastructure and cost ownership. You've owned a cost-attribution or compliance program end to end (control design, evidence collection, external audit such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, or comparable) for a production system on Kubernetes or similar.
Track record building and leading a focused engineering team, ideally growing a team from a handful of engineers rather than inheriting one at scale.
Experience balancing resource constraints. GPU capacity, region availability, and cost are active, managed constraints in this role, not abstractions.
Experience supporting external-facing or customer-facing deployments, not only internal research infrastructure.
Operational excellence in engineering teams and systems.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with common LLM-serving stacks (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Triton, SGLang, or similar).
Experience working with research and product stakeholders to define the engineering roadmap of a production system.
Exposure to GPU-cluster capacity planning or multi-region/multi-cloud deployment.
Familiarity with systems development languages (Rust, Go, etc.).
Exposure to a regulated or compliance-heavy production environment.

Even if you don't have all of the above requirements, we encourage you to apply to explore a mutual fit!

This posting is for proactive recruitment purposes and may be used to fill current openings or future vacancies within our organization.

What’s in it For You?

Hybrid Work Model: We’ve adopted a flexible hybrid working environment for our office-based roles while delivering a seamless experience that is digitally and physically connected.
Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. This builds upon our flexible work arrangements, including work from anywhere for up to 8 weeks per year, empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance.
Career Development and Growth: By fostering a culture of continuous learning and skill development, we prepare our talent to tackle tomorrow’s challenges and deliver real-world solutions. Our Grow My Way programming and skills-first approach ensures you have the tools and knowledge to grow, lead, and thrive in an AI-enabled future.
Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include flexible vacation, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.
Culture: Globally recognized, award-winning reputation for inclusion and belonging, flexibility, work-life balance, and more. We live by our values: Obsess over our Customers, Compete to Win, Challenge (Y)our Thinking, Act Fast / Learn Fast, and Stronger Together.
Social Impact: Make an impact in your community with our Social Impact Institute. We offer employees two paid volunteer days off annually and opportunities to get involved with pro-bono consulting projects and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives.
Making a Real-World Impact: We are one of the few companies globally that helps its customers pursue justice, truth, and transparency. Together, with the professionals and institutions we serve, we help uphold the rule of law, turn the wheels of commerce, catch bad actors, report the facts, and provide trusted, unbiased information to people all over the world.

Our use of AI within the recruitment process Thomson Reuters utilizes Artificial Intelligence (AI) to support parts of our global recruitment process. Unless you opt-out, our AI system will assess the information provided by you and compare it to the requirements listed for the role, and present the result to our recruitment personnel for further review. The AI system acts as a supporting tool, but there is always a human making the decision if you will be considered for the role.

In the United States, Thomson Reuters offers a comprehensive benefits package to our employees. Our benefit package includes market competitive health, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance programs, as well as a competitive 401k plan with company match. In addition, Thomson Reuters offers market leading work life benefits with competitive vacation, sick and safe paid time off, paid holidays (including two company mental health days off), parental leave, sabbatical leave. These benefits meet or exceeds the requirements of paid time off in accordance with any applicable state or municipal laws. Finally, Thomson Reuters offers the following additional benefits: optional hospital, accident and sickness insurance paid 100% by the employee; optional life and AD&D insurance paid 100% by the employee; Flexible Spending and Health Savings Accounts; fitness reimbursement; access to Employee Assistance Program; Group Legal Identity Theft Protection benefit paid 100% by employee; access to 529 Plan; commuter benefits; Adoption & Surrogacy Assistance; Tuition Reimbursement; and access to Employee Stock Purchase Plan.

Thomson Reuters complies with local laws that require upfront disclosure of the expected pay range for a position. The base compensation range varies across locations. Eligible office location(s) for this role include one or more of the following: New York City, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and/or Irvine, CA; McLean, VA; Washington, DC. The base compensation range for the role in any of those locations is $212,100 USD - $393,900 USD. For any eligible US locations, unless otherwise noted, the base compensation range for this role is $184,100 USD - $341,900 USD. Base pay is positioned within the range based on several factors including an individual’s knowledge, skills and experience with consideration given to internal equity. Base pay is one part of a comprehensive Total Reward program which also includes flexible and supportive benefits and other wellbeing programs. This role may also be eligible for an Annual Bonus based on a combination of enterprise and individual performance.

About Us

Thomson Reuters informs the way forward by bringing together the trusted content and technology that people and organizations need to make the right decisions. We serve professionals across legal, tax, accounting, compliance, government, and media. Our products combine highly specialized software and insights to empower professionals with the data, intelligence, and solutions needed to make informed decisions, and to help institutions in their pursuit of justice, truth, and transparency. Reuters, part of Thomson Reuters, is a world leading provider of trusted journalism and news.

We are powered by the talents of 26,000 employees across more than 70 countries, where everyone has a chance to contribute and grow professionally in flexible work environments. At a time when objectivity, accuracy, fairness, and transparency are under attack, we consider it our duty to pursue them. Sound exciting? Join us and help shape the industries that move society forward.

As a global business, we rely on the unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences of all employees to deliver on our business goals. To ensure we can do that, we seek talented, qualified employees in all our operations around the world regardless of race, color, sex/gender, including pregnancy, gender identity and expression, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, disability, age, marital status, citizen status, veteran status, or any other protected classification under applicable law. Thomson Reuters is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer providing a drug-free workplace.

Thomson Reuters makes reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities, including veterans with disabilities, and for sincerely held religious beliefs in accordance with applicable law. If you reside in the United States and require an accommodation in the recruiting process, you may contact our Human Resources Department at HR.Leave-Expert@thomsonreuters.com. Disability accommodations in the recruiting process may include things like a sign language interpreter, making interview rooms accessible, providing assistive technology, or other relevant accommodations. Please note this email is not intended for general recruitment questions and we will promptly respond to inquiries regarding accommodations. More information on requesting an accommodation here.

Learn more on how to protect yourself from fraudulent job postings here.

More information about Thomson Reuters can be found on thomsonreuters.com
